The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X∼N(5,{6}^{2}),$ compute $P(X<2).$ Use the table below and do not round your answer.

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-0.6\,$ | $\,0.2743\,$ | $\,0.2709\,$ | $\,0.2676\,$ |
| $\,-0.5\,$ | $\,0.3085\,$ | $\,0.3050\,$ | $\,0.3015\,$ |
| $\,-0.4\,$ | $\,0.3446\,$ | $\,0.3409\,$ | $\,0.3372\,$ |

$P(X<2)=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
Given a normal random variable $X∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),$ we have

$$
P(X<x)=P(Z<\frac{x-\mu }{\sigma })
$$

where $Z∼N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu =5$ and $\sigma =6.$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<2) & =P(Z<\frac{2-5}{6}) \\  & =P(Z<-0.5) \\  & =P(Z\le -0.5) \\  & =Φ(-0.5)\end{aligned}
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14070250/assets/6d13179aa11fed4255ce0997c71063a6398fdbb9c6124a4048c9a29759317ab8.png)

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(-0.5)=0.3085.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
P(X<2)=0.3085.
$$
